door.response: The Major Rock Edicts are fourteen separate inscriptions carved into in-situ rocks, attributed to Emperor Ashoka of the Mauryan Empire (r. c. 268–232 BCE). They are significantly detailed and among the earliest dated rock inscriptions of any Indian monarch, preceded chronologically by the Minor Rock Edicts. They sit within a larger collection of more than thirty inscriptions spread across pillars, boulders, and cave walls throughout the subcontinent.
